detail:
Mayo Clinic describes treatment of restless legs syndrome as beginning with any underlying condition: symptoms sometimes settle after a contributor such as iron deficiency is treated, which can involve iron supplementation by mouth or through a vein, taken only after blood-iron levels have been checked and under a clinician's monitoring. When RLS is not caused by another condition, Mayo Clinic describes lifestyle changes as the first focus, with prescription medicines considered when those measures are not effective.

Medicine classes Mayo Clinic lists include medicines affecting calcium channels, described as the first line of treatment for most people, medicines that increase dopamine in the brain for short-term use, and, for severe cases that have not responded to other options, opioid medicines. Mayo Clinic also describes a prescription device that delivers electrical stimulation to a nerve at the side of the knee. Self-care measures in the source include regular moderate exercise, consistent sleep habits, warm baths, leg massage, and reducing caffeine, alcohol, and nicotine.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about managing restless legs syndrome and its treatments.
summary: Mayo Clinic describes RLS management that starts with treating underlying contributors such as iron deficiency, moves through lifestyle changes, and adds prescription medicine classes or a nerve stimulation device when symptoms persist.
takeaways: treating contributors such as iron deficiency comes first in the source
lifestyle changes and sleep habits are the foundation before medicines
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Restless Legs Syndrome: managing symptoms, from iron checks to medicines
